races.name: Racing To School Celebrates 25 Years Lady Amateur Jockeys Handicap Stakes (For Female Amateur Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Little Empire
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong recent form over shorter trips at 7f, now stepping up to a mile at Ascot on good ground where her sim-going record of 4/15 shows limited but positive exposure; Miss A B O'Connor partnership fresh off 23 days, and the mile trip here is the key question for a horse with a history of 7f and 6f runs.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a second three starts back, Little Empire brings solid form into this and has run over today's trip and going before; winless in his last six starts is the caveat, but drawn in stall two and carrying 150 lb, he looks the one to beat on our ratings.

runners_data.name: Cancan In The Rain
runners_data.note: Six-year-old prominent type whose best sim-going record (1W4P from 15 runs) shows she handles good ground, and trainer Gihan Arnolda fires in at 1/8 over 14 days suggesting the yard is in form; headgear worn, 15 days since last run, and a trip profile mostly at 7f-8f makes this mile trip within range.
runners_data.comment: Cancan In The Rain has been consistently competitive in recent starts, finishing fourth three times and picking up a third last time out, and he returns in good order just 15 days on with distance and going experience in his favour; the concern is he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Stratocracy
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer trained by the Kevin & Lauren Frost partnership who have been active at 1/15 over 14 days; all five recent runs have come over 7f on good ground and she has placed five times from 15 similar-going runs, so the mile step-up is the principal unknown for Miss Lauren Frost aboard.
runners_data.comment: Stratocracy steps up as a leading danger on the back of a third two starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going is a solid foundation; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts and must prove he can convert promise into results from stall 7 off 145 lb.

runners_data.name: Dannick
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has won twice at 7f on standard going and whose sim-going exposure on good ground is very limited at just 2/15 runs; trainer Gary & Josh Moore are in excellent form at 3/31 over 14 days, and the switch from standard to good ground is the critical variable for this four-year-old who races off OR 73.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Dannick is hard to fancy at these weights, yet his recent form does show two wins in his last six starts, including a winner last time out, and he has run over today's trip before, while stall one is his draw.

runners_data.name: Atmosphere
runners_data.note: Patient, hold-up performer who has placed on good ground and on standard, with a visor in the locker and 50 days off the track — the significant freshness query in this field; Miss Georgia King takes the ride, and Atmosphere's best efforts have come from off the pace at 7f-8f, making her a genuine candidate if the prominent group tire.
runners_data.comment: Atmosphere has been a model of consistency, placing in four of his last five starts including back-to-back seconds, and he has experience of today's distance and going; the main risk is that he heads here fifty days between runs yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Calyxoh
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with all recent runs at 8f on good or standard going and a visor fitted; Patrick Morris sends her here at 1/12 over 14 days, and her consistent placing record (1W3P from 8 similar-going runs) makes her a solid fit for the mile on today's good surface.
runners_data.comment: Calyxoh has shown some consistency in recent starts, placing third twice in his last six, and has run over today's trip and going before; yet to win in that spell and carrying 141 lb from stall eight, he faces a stiff ask against a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Tex
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing a tongue-tie and pads who won over 7f on good ground recently and has strong claims at this mile trip; George Baker's yard is ticking at 1/9 over 14 days, and 10 runs out of 14 on similar going including a win and seven places makes Tex one of the better-credentialed hold-up runners for a late challenge.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and a winner three starts back, Tex has experience of today's trip and going to call on, and 30 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; however, that ninth two starts back is a concern, and 141 lb is a sizeable burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Eazy On The Eye
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner, confirmed to lead and set whatever tempo suits; only six days since her last run suggests Heather Main is happy with her, and a string of placed efforts (0W2P on good) over 7f-8f shows she is competitive at this level even if she hasn't won — her ability to dictate will define the entire race shape.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in her last three starts — all runner-up finishes — Eazy On The Eye arrives here just six days on from her latest effort, and has run over today's trip and going before, though she remains yet to win and her rating of 73 leaves her eighth of eleven ranked runners.

runners_data.name: Bold Suitor
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old whose natural inclination is to race prominently, though the congestion in the prominent zone means he's likely to be shuffled back from his preferred spot — his experience and a recent win at 7f on standard going are positives, but Craig Benton's 0/1 over 14 days and the softer OR 69 limit expectations if he can't secure his natural berth.
runners_data.comment: Bold Suitor has managed just one win in his last six starts, finishing sixth last time out, and our rating ranks him tenth of eleven in this field; he has run over today's trip and returns after 15 days, but there is little in the recent figures to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: The Bitter Moose
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who tends to finish in the placing brackets (3/3/3/11/4 recently) on standard or good ground, wearing a visor; Patrick Chamings is quiet at 0/8 over 14 days, and with the rear of the field congested she is unlikely to get the clean passage her style demands — her chance is real but dependent on gaps appearing late.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in his last three starts, The Bitter Moose arrives fit on 15 days' rest with distance and going experience to call on, though he remains winless in recent starts and his draw eleven and 137 lb burden are no small asks for a runner rated 68 officially.

runners_data.name: Port Louis
runners_data.note: Hold-up type at OR 63 with a tendency to fade in the finish — flagged explicitly for that — and recent form shows little encouragement over good ground; Bernard Llewellyn has been active at 1/12 over 14 days but only six days since her last run and a poor sim-going record of 0W2P from 15 runs leaves her as the most vulnerable runner in the field if the race unfolds without an obvious opening.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a pair of eighths in his two most recent outings, Port Louis faces a stiff task from stall ten carrying 132 lb, and a rating of 60 ranked last of the field offers little encouragement, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Eazy On The Eye is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press her for the lead, she is set to control this mile at whatever tempo she chooses on good ground at Ascot. That uncontested position means she can dictate a measured, sustainable gallop, which on this flat mile with its straight finish will likely produce a steadily-run race with the decisive move coming in the final two furlongs. The tactical verdict is clear: a single, uncontested pace-setter on a flat, fair surface with a genuine cruising role strongly favours horses who can race prominently close to that controlled pace, striking before the hold-up horses have time to close — the prominent style profile is best placed here. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than can all secure their natural positions; Bold Suitor is a true prominent racer most likely to actually push forward, while The Bitter Moose and Port Louis, though genuine hold-up horses, are mapped to midfield due to congestion at the rear and are unlikely to get the clean, late run their style demands.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Eazy On The Eye Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Eazy On The Eye sets a comfortable solo lead and the field settles without any horse forcing the pace higher.
scenarios.body: Eazy On The Eye dictates a measured tempo throughout, reaching the straight with a clear-headed rhythm and reserves to extend; horses racing just behind her — Little Empire, Cancan In The Rain, Calyxoh — get the ideal prominent position to pounce in the final furlong without having to make up ground. This controlled shape suits the prominent profile best, as the pace is neither too fast to burn them out nor too slow to allow late closers a meaningful target.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Eazy On The Eye sets the pace but two prominent racers track her closely and overwhelm her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Stratocracy or Cancan In The Rain press up to Eazy On The Eye from halfway, turning the race into a sustained test of stamina in the straight where the best-handicapped prominent horse wins; horses who have been travelling kindly just off the pace have the positional advantage over any hold-up runners. This scenario rewards horses proven over a mile on good ground with a prominent racing style, which Little Empire and Calyxoh also fit well.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses early enough to give Atmosphere, Tex, or Dannick a clear late run through a well-strung-out field.
scenarios.body: A steady pace paradoxically creates a slingshot for the hold-up horses only if the prominent group use each other up fighting for position; Atmosphere and Tex, both proven on good ground at this sort of trip, have the class and form to deliver a late flourish if gaps appear. Note that The Bitter Moose and Port Louis, though mapped to midfield, are genuine hold-up types racing out of their preferred role and carry reduced chance in this shape — Atmosphere and Tex are the true candidates here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Bold Suitor Forces Forward
scenarios.trigger: If Bold Suitor pushes into a genuine prominent position and combines with Eazy On The Eye to create an unexpectedly contested pace.
scenarios.body: Bold Suitor is a true prominent racer mapped to midfield due to field congestion, but if he manages to assert his natural position he raises the tempo and forces a stronger gallop that tests all horses' stamina in the straight. At OR 69 and age nine with course form, this outcome is unlikely given how crowded the prominent berths are, making this the lowest-probability shape.

watchPoints.text: Eazy On The Eye — watch whether she goes clear from the front or is tracked closely from the outset, as the size of her lead by halfway will determine whether any hold-up horse has a realistic chance of closing.

Bold Suitor — a true prominent racer who may attempt to push forward despite the crowded pace positions; if he forces his way up to Eazy On The Eye before halfway he could raise the tempo unexpectedly and punish horses who have gone too early.

Atmosphere — 50 days off the track is the longest layoff in the field and she was last seen wearing a visor, so watch in the paddock for signs of freshness or ring-rustiness that could affect her ability to produce a clean late run.

Dannick — almost all recent runs on standard going rather than good, so observe his early action and whether he settles smoothly; if the going is riding quicker than expected his chance will depend on whether he handles the transition.

The Bitter Moose and Port Louis — both genuine hold-up types operating in a congested midfield rather than their natural rear position; if the field fans wide in the straight it could give them a run, but watch whether they find themselves trapped on the rail with nowhere to go.

races.name: Charbonnel et Walker EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Ascot Events EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Juddmonte Ebf Restricted Novice Stakes (for Horses In Bands A, B, C And D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qual) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Pure Mint
runners_data.note: Won her only start over this exact trip and going at Newbury; Simon & Ed Crisford in fine recent form (1/20 last 14 days), James Doyle provides a strong jockey booking, and 39 days between runs is not a concern for a lightly-raced juvenile with a clean profile.

runners_data.name: Soldier Of The Sea
runners_data.note: Back-to-back 6f Good-ground runs yielding a win and a second mark her as the standout hold-up/prominent performer by consistency; Taylor Fisher is an apprentice claim-carrier which may help in a race where weight is equal at 136lbs, and William Knight's 4/15 strike rate over 14 days shows yard in form.

runners_data.name: Does Mary Know
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's form figure of 62 (beaten second on Good ground, then sixth) reflects a horse whose best may need a different race shape — she is a natural hold-up type who will find herself racing closer to the pace than ideal given the single front-runner scenario, which tempers confidence despite her OR of 120.

runners_data.name: Nobelos
runners_data.note: Ran on into fourth on his only start on Good ground at 6f; Charles Hills is a 3/18 trainer in the last 14 days so the yard is ticking over, and Rob Hornby is a reliable claimer, but a single run showing no win or place record means he remains very much unexposed.

runners_data.name: War Chest
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed on debut with no form line to assess; headgear (hg=h) fitted for a first start suggests connections are looking to sharpen his focus, and Eve Johnson Houghton's 3/30 recent rate is modest, making this an intriguing but high-risk runner at an unknown going suitability.

runners_data.name: Storm Force Ten
runners_data.note: Ran a decent third at 6f Good ground last time before a forgettable effort on Tapeta at 7f; Saffie Osborne's booking is notable given the conditional allowance, but his form base is thin and Jamie Osborne's 2/13 yard strike rate is only moderate — best treated as a place contender at best.

runners_data.name: Brushstroke
runners_data.note: Runner-up at 7f on Tapeta on his only start is the entirety of his profile; a step down to 6f on turf is the unknown variable, but a prominent running style means Ray Dawson can position him just off Pure Mint and leverage the pace shape — the trip shortening could suit or expose him.

races.paceDynamic: Pure Mint is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a seven-runner field, she can dictate from the front at a pace entirely of her own choosing over this straight Ascot 6f. Brushstroke and Soldier Of The Sea will press from prominent positions just off the pace, creating a two-deep early order but without the aggression to truly pressurise Pure Mint through the first two furlongs. Does Mary Know is a natural hold-up horse who has been redistributed to the midfield visual because this race shape pushes true closers back — the field contains more prominent/hold-up types than the map can accommodate, and Does Mary Know is the runner most likely racing out of her preferred role, with Pure Mint and Brushstroke the ones who will actually secure their natural positions. A sustainable, front-runner-controlled tempo over a flat, straight track on Good ground overwhelmingly favours the leader and those racing close to an uncontested pace — hold-up horses face the stiffest task and their prospects are materially discounted.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pure Mint Leads Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Mint breaks well and controls the pace from the front at a comfortable tempo, she dictates every yard of the 6f.
scenarios.body: She sets a measured but honest gallop that stretches the field through the dip and quickens clear inside the final furlong, never seriously threatened having conserved energy throughout; her solo win on Good ground at this trip is the form blueprint.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Brushstroke or Soldier Of The Sea use their prominent position to peg back Pure Mint in the final 2f when the pace eases.
scenarios.body: A slight slowdown mid-race brings the front pair into range of the leader, allowing a horse with tactical speed travelling just off the pace to collared Pure Mint near the line; Soldier Of The Sea's consistent 6f Good-ground form makes her the most credible beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Mint sets a genuinely strong early gallop that burns out the prominent runners and opens the race up for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected pace collapses the front end inside the final furlong, allowing a horse from the rear to sprint through beaten rivals; Nobelos or Storm Force Ten, tracking off the pace, would be the theoretical beneficiaries though both are racing in a position that is less natural for this race shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutant Lands Big Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If War Chest, making his racecourse debut, shows exceptional natural ability and threads through from an unpredictable position.
scenarios.body: An unknown quantity can sometimes outclass experienced rivals on raw talent alone, and hg=h headgear on debut may sharpen focus; however, the complete absence of a form line and an unknown going preference make this the highest-risk scenario.

watchPoints.text: Pure Mint's gate break is the pivotal moment — if she misses the kick and another runner takes the lead, the entire race dynamic inverts and hold-up horses immediately become more viable.

Does Mary Know is a natural hold-up horse who will be ridden closer to the pace than normal in this race shape; watch for Charles Bishop choosing to drop her out regardless, which would leave her needing a dramatically strong pace to materialise.
War Chest debuts with headgear fitted — watch the market move in the hour before the race as any significant support would signal stable confidence in a runner whose ability is completely unknown.

Soldier Of The Sea is one of only two runners with multiple runs on Good ground at 6f and has placed both times; if Pure Mint is beaten, she is the most likely alternative result and her market price relative to her form record is worth monitoring.

Storm Force Ten's previous run came just 14 days ago on an artificial surface — watch whether he strips fitter or slightly jaded on return to turf, as his freshness will determine whether he can sustain his effort into the final furlong.

races.name: Big Ascot Food & Wine Festival Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Aalto
runners_data.note: Has winning and placed form across multiple 7f Good-ground races at this trip (1W4P in 11 similar runs), making the conditions genuinely ideal; hold-up style suits a race with a controlled leader but requires a proper run through the pack — James Doyle's fitness advantage after 41 days off should be respected.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a winner two starts back, Aalto arrives in solid recent form and has run over today's trip and going, giving him a familiar test; 41 days between runs is worth a note, but the consistent profile makes him our pick from stall four carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Best Rate
runners_data.note: Consistent at a mile on Good but stepping back to 7f with all five recent runs over 8f — the trip shortening is a question mark; a natural pace-pressing type whose instinct to race prominently will be curtailed by the number of similar horses in this field, and Seamus Cronin's 5lb claim only partially compensates for racing against the grain tactically.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back and a winner on each of the two occasions before that, Best Rate has distance and going experience to call on and arrives fresh enough on nine days' rest; the cold trainer streak — no wins in 42 attempts over 14 days — is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Jolly Roger
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride for the Crisfords on a horse with five consecutive placed finishes including two at 7f on Good; 137 days off (tongue-tie noted) is the only concern, but the prominent racing style maps perfectly to what this race shape requires and the class of jockey is a major plus.
runners_data.comment: Jolly Roger has been a model of consistency, placing second three times and third once in his last five starts, and he has run over today's trip and going before — yet to win in that spell is the concern, and a trainer firing at just 5% over the last 14 days adds to the risk.

runners_data.name: Jonny Concrete
runners_data.note: A five-year-old in sharp form with four wins from his last six including two at 7f Good — by ability he is firmly in contention; naturally wants to race prominently but the number of pace-pressing rivals makes that position difficult to secure cleanly, meaning his best form may not be fully reproducible in this specific race shape unless he can assert early.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins give Jonny Concrete solid recent momentum and he has run over today's trip and going before, but carrying 135 lb from stall six against stronger company — rated a pound below his official mark — may blunt his chance here.

runners_data.name: Veblen Good
runners_data.note: Six straight runs without a win and a move from 6f to 7f is not obviously strengthening the case for this David O'Meara runner; Tom Marquand is a booking of note but the recent form figures (0,3,3,4,4) on Good ground at shorter trips leave the question of whether the extra furlong will unlock improvement rather than expose a horse that needs a different set of circumstances.
runners_data.comment: Veblen Good is the top-rated runner in this field and returns quickly on a seven-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and conditions in his favour, yet he remains winless in his last six starts, and that elusive breakthrough is the key question.

runners_data.name: Debrief
runners_data.note: The only genuine front-runner in the field and has won back-to-back on Good ground, both at 6f — stepping up to 7f is the key unknown for a 3-year-old who has faced faster early fractions at shorter; an uncontested lead is virtually guaranteed given the field composition, which neutralises his stamina query somewhat.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Debrief is hard to fancy despite back-to-back wins in his last two starts; the 41-day absence adds another question, though he has experience of today's trip and going, and draws stall three.

runners_data.name: Malachy's Wish
runners_data.note: Hold-up style is genuinely suited to a well-run race but all three Good-ground runs have produced modest results (2nd-best figures came on Standard ground), giving real cause for concern on going that has not brought out the best in this 3-year-old; Saffie Osborne retains the ride for her father and the 7f trip looks right in theory.
runners_data.comment: Malachy's Wish won two starts back and was runner-up last time out, showing he retains form, but his speed rating of 85 trails the top-ranked rivals and two unplaced efforts in recent starts hint at inconsistency on the way back to that winning return.

runners_data.name: Suspicious Mindz
runners_data.note: Two wins in last four including back-to-back victories at 7f and 6f on Good ground — this horse is progressive and in excellent form; a prominent racer who has found the right trip and conditions, and Dale Swift's experience at the track is useful, though the step up from maiden/novice company into a classified race tests its ceiling.
runners_data.comment: Suspicious Mindz has won twice in his last five starts, most recently a winner last time out, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions, but our rating has him well held on these terms and he faces a stiff task from the top of the weights at 131 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Debrief is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should coast to a comfortable, uncontested position from the outset, setting a sustainable gallop over Ascot's straight seven furlongs on Good ground. Jolly Roger, Veblen Good, and Suspicious Mindz will press for prominent spots just behind, creating a structured race rather than a scramble, while Aalto and Malachy's Wish will settle in rear to make late bids. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Jonny Concrete and Best Rate are natural prominent horses who will likely find themselves shuffled into midfield against their instincts, diluting their effectiveness. The uncontested, controlled tempo that Debrief is set to create strongly favours those who can travel prominently in a compressed pack and quicken from there, rather than horses making up ground from the back on what figures to be a non-gruelling gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Debrief Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Debrief dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the race is decided in the final two furlongs by those who tracked closely.
scenarios.body: Debrief sets a measured fractions from the front, and horses racing in second or third gear just off the pace — Jolly Roger and Suspicious Mindz — find themselves perfectly placed to launch their challenges; the hold-up horses are left with insufficient ground to make up in a race that never truly accelerates into a genuine test.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debrief Wins Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely slow and Debrief's rivals fail to pick up sufficiently, leaving the leader to score on his own terms.
scenarios.body: Debrief's uncontested lead becomes an unanswerable advantage as rivals either hit traffic or find the finishing kick simply not there on a Good surface that rewards relaxed gallopers; a 3-year-old who has won two of his last two on Good ground, he has the profile to dictate and simply not be caught.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively strong early and the front rank fades, allowing the hold-up horses to pick them off close home.
scenarios.body: Aalto has recent winning form over this exact trip and going (7f, Good) and Malachy's Wish, despite limited Good-ground form, would benefit from a strongly-run race that brings stamina into play; both have the profile to emerge from the pack if the race develops into a proper test in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Cause Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Jonny Concrete or Best Rate manage to force their way into a prominent position early, creating pace pressure that disrupts the anticipated race shape.
scenarios.body: A fractious early battle for position would compress the field and potentially unsettle Debrief's rhythm, opening the race to a more unpredictable finish; however, given both horses are likely to be squeezed out of their natural role, this remains the least probable scenario.

watchPoints.text: Jolly Roger's 137-day absence is the single biggest risk to the race result — watch for signs of rustiness in the paddock or a rough early jump, as William Buick's booking suggests connections are confident but fitness is genuinely unproven.

Jonny Concrete and Best Rate will both try to press forward from their likely starting positions — watch the first two furlongs for a scramble among the prominent types that could disrupt Debrief's ideal uncontested lead.

Malachy's Wish has zero wins or places from seven runs on Good ground — if the going description is accurate and not faster, the hold-up horse faces a meaningful profile mismatch that could see Saffie Osborne struggling to get competitive.

Debrief is dropping back from a 6f win to 7f for the first time — watch the closing stages to see whether stamina becomes a factor and whether Aalto or Suspicious Mindz can reel in the leader if the gallop has been genuinely sustainable throughout.

Best Rate's trainer Richard Hannon has had zero wins from 42 runners over the last 14 days — a notable cold-spell that tempers the expectation around an already tactically compromised ride for Seamus Cronin.

races.name: Ascot Hospitality Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Blue Rc
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with four second-place finishes at the mile on Good; Rob Hornby positive booking, James Tate in solid 14-day form (3/14), 41 days since last run is fine — needs to hold its prominent slot against traffic.|
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back seconds before a winner two starts further back in recent form, Blue Rc brings solid placed consistency to this; he has run over today's trip and going, and a 41-day break should leave him fresh, with our rating of 108 marking him the one to beat from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Classic
runners_data.note: Six-year-old holding strong Good-ground form at the mile (13/15 sim-going runs placed); Pat Dobbs rides for Hannon who is having a quieter spell (0/42 in 14 days), but the horse's profile at this course and trip is undeniable.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out after a spell of poor efforts, Classic has run over today's trip and going and his rating of 104 suggests he holds strong claims; the concern is a trainer without a winner in 42 recent attempts.

runners_data.name: Hard Endeavor
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan partners this Chapple-Hyam runner returning after 62 days — the layoff is the main flag; placed twice at the mile on Good and ran well fresh last time, so the break may not be damaging, but the competitive prominent division is a challenge.|
runners_data.comment: Ran well to finish second last time out, though a mixed recent record includes one unplaced effort and 62 days off adds a fitness query; has run over today's trip and going, and 136 lb from stall 3 makes him a solid if unspectacular mid-market proposition.

runners_data.name: Urban Lion
runners_data.note: Returned a win at the mile on Soft last time but most of his Good-ground mile runs have been disappointing; George Bass is an apprentice booking in a competitive handicap, and the wide field (13 runners) could make his prominent style harder to execute.|
runners_data.comment: Urban Lion won four starts back, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; however, his two most recent outings have yielded a ninth and an unplaced effort, and recapturing that form after 41 days off is the key question.

runners_data.name: Ozat
runners_data.note: James Doyle rides this Ian Williams hold-up type who has placed at the trip on Good going; the headgear flag (t) suggests he needs settling, and Doyle's ability to place him correctly from a hold-up position in a pace-contested race is a key advantage.|
runners_data.comment: Ozat has run over today's trip and going, and a rating of 104 ranks him second of thirteen, marking him out as a genuine danger; the risk is that he's winless in his last six starts, with only a third last time out to cling to.

runners_data.name: Arctic Thunder
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at the mile on Good going confirm his strong affinity for today's conditions; Ashley Lewis claims 3lb which is useful at the weights, and Ed Walker's stable is in fine form (7/43 in 14 days) — a genuine hold-up horse who suits this pace dynamic.|
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins make Arctic Thunder interesting, though he rates only eighth of the 13 on our figures, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions, but an official mark of 96 and 132 lb from stall two asks him to defy a stern weight burden against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Hickory
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a large number of runs at the mile on Good (12/15 sim-going); Saffie Osborne rides, headgear flag (p) present, and while he won at the trip on Good last summer, his recent form figures (0,6,0,6,1,5) are patchy — needs the pace to collapse in the straight.|
runners_data.comment: Hickory landed a win two starts back but has finished fifth most recently, and his record in the last six starts shows just that single success; experience over today's trip and going helps, though 131 lb from stall 11 is no gimme.

runners_data.name: Spanish Voice
runners_data.note: One of two confirmed front-runners with three wins at the mile on Good — Colin Keane, an elite jockey, gives him a major tactical edge in controlling the pace from the front; Andrew Balding's stable is in excellent form (12/56 in 14 days), making him the more dangerous of the two leaders.|
runners_data.comment: Spanish Voice was third last time out but has been beaten into fifth and unplaced in between his two wins in recent starts, and ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures he faces a stiff task off 130 lb from stall one, though he does at least have experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Witch Hunter
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose one win at the mile on Good shows the profile is there; recent form is modest (0,0,0,1,0,6) and the 20-day turnaround is quick — needs Spanish Voice or Moonfall to really set it up and rivals to tire ahead of him.|
runners_data.comment: Witch Hunter won three starts back but has posted two unplaced efforts since, and a trainer currently without a winner in 42 attempts is a clear negative; he has run over today's trip and going, and 130 lb from stall 4 keeps him in the picture without inspiring confidence.

runners_data.name: Moonfall
runners_data.note: Three-year-old carrying 128lbs and confirmed front-runner; Jack Callan is the booking for Boughey (4/31 in 14 days) and all seven of his Good-going runs have come at Good, showing no going concern — the question is whether he can live with Spanish Voice's pace before tiring.|
runners_data.comment: Moonfall won two starts back but was fourth last time out after 55 days off the track, so fitness is a fair question; he has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 102 suggests residual ability, though draw 12 and 128 lb are not without challenge.

runners_data.name: Jolly Jack Tar
runners_data.note: William Buick is a significant jockey upgrade for the Gosden yard (6/20 in 14 days), but 402 days off the track is a severe fitness question at this level; his best form has come over 10 furlongs and this mile trip may be tight — treat as a watch-and-learn runner.|
runners_data.comment: A lengthy 402-day absence and a ranking of 12 of 13 on our figures make Jolly Jack Tar difficult to fancy on return, though he has run over today's distance and going before, and a trainer firing at 30% in the last 14 days at least offers some encouragement.

runners_data.name: Zennor Storm
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides this Haggas runner (9/49 in 14 days, strong form) who is a genuine prominent racer in reality — the crowded prominent division means he is unlikely to get his preferred position, and racing out of role from a midfield slot tempers his chance despite the smart yard.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 11 of 13 on our figures, Zennor Storm faces a stiff ask here; an eighth last time out does little to encourage, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Mythical Guest
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by nature, mapped to midfield only because the rear of the field is as congested as the front; OR of 78 represents a significant class underdog in this field, and even if the race sets up for late closers his figures (0W3P in 11 Good-going runs) suggest placing rather than winning.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Mythical Guest faces a stiff task from stall 13, though he has shown some consistency in his last three outings and has experience of today's distance and going.

races.paceDynamic: Moonfall and Spanish Voice are confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the off over Ascot's straight mile, creating a genuinely contested pace on Good ground rather than a comfortable lone-leader scenario. With four prominent horses — Blue Rc, Classic, Hard Endeavor, Urban Lion — also pressing to race close to the pace, the gallop should be honest and sustained throughout, compressing the advantage for those who lead. This contested dynamic historically favours horses who can sit just off the speed in the first four or five and quicken from a position of cover, meaning prominent-to-midfield closers with a late gear are best placed. The field contains more front-running and prominent horses than can all secure their natural positions — Blue Rc, Classic, Hard Endeavor, and Urban Lion are most likely to actually hold the prominent slots, while Zennor Storm and Mythical Guest, both genuine pace-pressing or hold-up types in reality, have been redistributed to midfield in the map because the race shape has no room for them in their preferred positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Moonfall and Spanish Voice fight it out up front and the pace holds honest all the way, softening the leaders.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off at an honest clip, leaving the prominent-to-midfield runners with cover to peel out and finish strongly in the straight; Arctic Thunder and Ozat, both holding-up types with strong Good-ground form at the trip, are ideally suited to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner (likely Spanish Voice or Moonfall) settles the early battle and the others concede ground, allowing a prominent racer to track and pounce.
scenarios.body: The pace becomes honest but not brutal, and a horse sitting second or third with cover — Blue Rc or Classic — can produce a sustained challenge in the Ascot straight without over-committing; both have strong form on Good going at the mile and suit a race where the early speed is absorbed rather than obliterated.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Spanish Voice or Moonfall secures a clear lead early and the contested spell is brief, allowing one to find a rhythm and prove strongest staying on.
scenarios.body: Ascot's straight mile can reward a front-runner who gets into their stride quickly and doesn't over-race in the first half; Spanish Voice's three wins at the trip on Good and strong trainer form (12/56 in 14 days) make this the more credible of the two pace-setters to hold on.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly scorching and the field strings out, creating a race that sets up for horses launching late runs from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Hickory and Witch Hunter are genuine hold-up types with good profiles at the mile on Good ground, but both carry moderate recent form figures and this shape depends on a faster pace than the Good going and 13-runner field will typically generate; the redistributed Mythical Guest is a true hold-up horse but its OR of 78 and limited winning profile makes winning this shape unlikely even if it suits stylistically.

watchPoints.text: Moonfall and Spanish Voice — watch which one blinks first in the early duel; if Colin Keane pressures Moonfall hard from the gates, the pace could be genuinely fast, which would sharply increase the chance of a hold-up horse (Arctic Thunder, Ozat) winning.

Jolly Jack Tar — William Buick on a 402-day absentee is an enormous wildcard; watch for market moves, as Buick rarely rides without expectation and the Gosden yard may know more than the formbook suggests.

Zennor Storm — despite being shown in midfield on the map, Tom Marquand may attempt to force his way up to his natural prominent position in a 13-runner field; if he succeeds it adds another body to an already congested early pace, making Scenario A even more likely.

Arctic Thunder — both of his most recent wins have come at the mile on Good going; if Ashley Lewis gets a clean run from his hold-up position without being blocked in a 13-runner field, he is the textbook beneficiary of the likely pace scenario.

Hickory — headgear flag (p) and Saffie Osborne's low-key booking suggest connections are hoping for a clean run in a strongly run race; monitor pre-race market drift or support as a signal to whether the yard expects conditions to suit today.

races.name: Sodexo Live! Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: First Legion
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with consistent placed form on Good ground, though six runs without a win at this level raises the question of whether he finds enough — Richard Hannon's yard has had no winners from 42 runners over the past 14 days, adding further caution.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts and returning after 83 days with a trainer who has yet to land a winner in 42 attempts over the past fortnight, First Legion faces questions — though he has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 101 puts him clear of his rivals.

runners_data.name: Raging Raj
runners_data.note: Legitimate prominent racer in excellent recent form with two wins from his last four outings over 7f on Good ground — the trip and conditions are ideal, and trainer Herrington has a recent winner from 11 runners; the key question is whether he handles the pace contest smoothly from a tracking position.|
runners_data.comment: Raging Raj arrives on the back of a win last time out, and a winner three starts back too, bringing a sharp two-from-six recent run of form into this; he has experience of today's trip and going, and the 135 lb burden is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Luansobe
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won over this exact 7f trip on Standard ground but has been inconsistent on Good, with a heavy fall back through the field on his last Good-ground run; Charlie Fellowes has a winner from 14 recent runners and the 55-day break warrants monitoring.|
runners_data.comment: Luansobe won three starts back and was third last time out, showing he can mix it at this level, though two unplaced efforts in between temper enthusiasm; he has run over today's trip and going, and returns after 55 days carrying 132 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Hambelton
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner whose last three starts include two wins over 8f on Good ground — dropping to 7f could sharpen his finishing effort and he has the profile of a horse that makes life hard for rivals if he gets daylight early; trainer Marnane has a recent winner from 14 runners.|
runners_data.comment: Hambelton arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, though two fifth-place finishes in his last six starts temper enthusiasm; carrying 132 lb from stall four after 41 days off, he maps as a genuine each-way contender rather than a banker.

runners_data.name: Star Of Commala
runners_data.note: Front-runner with two wins from three outings, though all form was recorded on Standard ground — this will be her first start on Good turf and the 7-pound claimer on board adds uncertainty, though the pace she generates will shape the entire race regardless of her finishing position.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Star Of Commala faces a stiff ask, but back-to-back wins in her last two starts suggest she arrives in career-best form; she has run over today's trip and returns on a quick 15-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Golden Brown
runners_data.note: Prominent type who has shown form from the front over 6f but steps up to 7f here — Tom Marquand is a high-class booking and Ed Walker's yard has been strong with seven winners from 43 recent runners; the extra furlong on Good ground is the live question to resolve.|
runners_data.comment: Golden Brown landed a win three starts back and arrives here fit on 23 days' rest, with experience of today's trip and going and a rating of 93 suggesting he holds strong claims; the risk is that two modest finishes since that victory must give pause.

runners_data.name: Sapphire Steps
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been out of the frame across all eight career runs on Good going — the form figures of 7-5840 are uninspiring and Richard Hannon's 14-day record of 0/42 across the stable compounds the concern; requires a dramatic change of fortune.|
runners_data.comment: Sapphire Steps showed enough ability when fourth two starts back to suggest she retains potential, and our rating of 88 marks her as a serious player, but a 56-day absence combined with a trainer in the depths of a lengthy losing run makes confidence hard to hold.

runners_data.name: King Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse returning from 120 days off, which is a significant flag — his one win came on Soft ground and his Good-ground form shows 6/7f/GOO without placing; James Doyle is an obvious positive but the layoff and going record create real doubt about fitness and conditions.|

runners_data.name: You Sexy Thing
runners_data.note: Has won twice on Soft ground and hit the frame over this trip, but his natural hold-up style is compressed here by the volume of other rearward horses — racing essentially out of his preferred position, his STYLE_FIT score of 0.91 reflects genuine tactical disadvantage in this shape, and the 85-day break adds further reservation.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of eight on our figures, You Sexy Thing makes little appeal after finishing sixth and unplaced in his last two, and his sole recent win came four starts back; the experience over today's trip and going, plus a third three starts back, are slim consolations after 85 days off.

races.paceDynamic: Star Of Commala and Hambelton are the two confirmed front-runners in this nine-runner 7f handicap, and with both likely to press for the early lead, this race will be run at an honest, contested gallop from the outset — neither is the type to concede the rail without a fight. The pace battle between them should ensure the tempo is genuine rather than false, meaning the race will not be run in a pocket-shuffle style that hands an advantage to hold-up horses late. On Good ground at Ascot over 7f, a genuine pace scenario of this kind classically stretches the field and sets up for horses who can travel prominently without burning too much fuel — prominent-style horses with tactical versatility are the primary beneficiaries. The field contains more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear, meaning You Sexy Thing is shown in midfield despite being a genuine hold-up horse — in a genuinely contested race, that redistribution is likely to cost rather than help.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Star Of Commala and Hambelton fight for the front and set a genuine honest gallop, prominent-to-midfield horses with stamina for the trip inherit the advantage.
scenarios.body: The front two burn each other up through the first half of the race, and those sitting just off the pace in the slipstream — travelling within themselves — are best placed to pounce from the 2f pole. Raging Raj and Golden Brown, both legitimate prominent types with course-appropriate form, are ideally profiled for a shape that rewards position and a strong finish over the final quarter.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Hambelton gets to the front uncontested and Star Of Commala settles without pressing, Hambelton can dictate on his own terms at a regulated pace.
scenarios.body: Hambelton has recent winning form over further on Good ground and is bred to stay, meaning if he gets a soft lead he can control the fractions and prove very difficult to reel in. His trainer has a recent winner and the horse's form figures of 121 at the top of the card give him strong claims if granted daylight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Fliers Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly brutal and the front two tire dramatically, genuine closers get the run of the race through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: First Legion and King Of Thunder are the truest hold-up horses, though both carry concerns — First Legion has been consistent without winning and King Of Thunder has had 120 days off. A strong pace collapse is needed and the Good ground may not produce that level of attrition.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, False Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner fully commits and the pace is slower than expected, the race bunches and becomes a dash from 2f out.
scenarios.body: This shape would be the least predictable outcome given two genuine speed horses are present, but if it occurs, a horse with a sharp turn of foot and good position like Golden Brown or Luansobe could benefit from the sprint-finish dynamic. This scenario requires an atypical tactical failure from the two pace horses and is therefore the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: Star Of Commala and Hambelton are both confirmed front-runners — watch the opening two furlongs closely to see whether they engage in a genuine duel or one cedes early, as this single factor will determine the entire pace shape and which profile wins.

King Of Thunder returns from 120 days off for Hugo Palmer — if he shows any signs of greenness or lack of fitness in the preliminaries, treat him with significant caution despite James Doyle's presence.

You Sexy Thing is a genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to the crowded rear of the field — if Saffie Osborne attempts to push forward out of role, watch for the horse to run below his best as a result of that positional compromise.

Golden Brown steps up from 6f to 7f for the first time on Good ground — how Tom Marquand positions him in the early stages will signal whether the yard believes the extra furlong is within his stamina range; a prominent pitch early would be a confident indicator.
